title: Desk Guidance on the Expiry of Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Company Points
content:
Company points of a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement expire by earning month.

**Rule.** Points earned in a calendar month expire at the end of the month that falls the tier's points-expiry period, in calendar months, after the month of earning, if they are still unredeemed. Redemptions always use the oldest unexpired points first. Expired points are posted in one expiry entry per earning month and are never reinstated. On termination, points not redeemed within the tier's post-termination redemption period, in calendar days after termination, expire at the end of that period, whatever their earning month.

**Points due to expire.** For an earning month whose validity has ended on or before the day in question, the points due to expire are the points earned in that month — accruals and bonuses, placed in the month of their posting date — less the redemptions allocated to that month oldest-first, and less any expiry already posted for that month.

### Worked dates and figures (hypothetical)

- With a points-expiry period of 24 months, points earned in March of one year expire at the end of March two years later.
- An agreement earned 1000 points in January and 500 points in February and has since redeemed 1200 points. The redemption used the oldest points first: all 1000 January points and 200 February points. If both months' validity has ended and no expiry has yet been posted for them, the points due to expire are 0 for January and 300 for February.
- An expiry already posted for an earning month reduces what remains due for that month; posted expiries are never reversed.
- An agreement is terminated on 1 June with a post-termination redemption period of 90 calendar days. Points still unredeemed at the end of that period expire then, even points earned in a month whose ordinary validity would have run longer.
